prompt.brief: Design a frontend-to-backend file downloader that supports resumable range requests, progress, integrity checks, cancellation, retries, and safe handling of changing or unauthorized resources.
successSignals: Define a download manifest with URL, length, ETag or version, chunk ranges, checksums, and destination state.
Use bounded concurrent range requests, resumable checkpoints, request cancellation, and exponential backoff.
Validate content length, ETag, hash, and safe filename before assembling the file; restart when the source changes.
Explain signed URLs, redirects, quotas, partial responses, disk exhaustion, browser limits, and corrupted chunks.

functional: Create a download, discover range support, fetch chunks, verify them, assemble the destination, and report progress.
Support pause, resume, cancellation, retry, concurrency adjustment, checksum verification, and changed-source detection.
Protect credentials and signed URLs, prevent path traversal, enforce file-size limits, and clean up partial state.
nonFunctional: Resume after network interruption without restarting completed ranges and expose progress within one chunk interval.
Bound concurrent connections and disk buffers per download, user, origin, and browser tab.
Persist checkpoints and verify every chunk; make retries safe and never overwrite a valid destination silently.
Fall back to one stream or pause with a resumable state when range support, storage, or the origin is degraded.
scaleAssumptions: Support 100,000 concurrent downloads, files from 1 MB to 1 TB, and unreliable mobile networks.
Partition state by download ID and origin; cap chunks, sockets, memory, and disk reservations per user.
Retain only resumable manifests and checksums; clean partial chunks after an explicit idle retention window.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Frontend-to-backend file downloader commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Frontend-to-backend file downloader writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Frontend-to-backend file downloader version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Frontend-to-backend file downloader by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Frontend-to-backend file downloader work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Frontend-to-backend file downloader projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Frontend-to-backend file downloader projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Frontend-to-backend file downloader records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Frontend-to-backend file downloader latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines source validation, ranged transfer, resume, integrity, scale, durability, and failure contracts.
Entities and job/source/chunk keys support resumable transfer, integrity, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Frontend-to-backend file downloader consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
